jobs.title: Engineering Manager / Tech Lead | Ethena Labs

requirements.text: Led engineering for consumer money product
requirements.quote: You’ve led engineering for a consumer money product — a neobank, payments, or crypto money app - where a bug moves or loses real customer money.

requirements.text: Led small team and shipped code
requirements.quote: You’ve led a small team (~3–8) while still shipping code yourself — tech lead, staff, or hands-on engineering manager.

requirements.text: Owned production operations for money system
requirements.quote: You’ve owned production operations for a money system — on-call, real incidents, observability, secret and key hygiene — not just delegated it.

You’ve owned, or overseen the integration of, regulated third-party financial rails — at least two of: card issuing / BIN-sponsor programs (Marqeta, Lithic, Kulipa, Stripe Issuing), identity / KYC / onboarding (SumSub, Persona, Onfido), banking or fiat on-/off-ramp partners (a BaaS or ramp partner), and key custody / signing (cloud KMS, HSM, MPC, or multisig).
alternatives: card issuing / BIN-sponsor programs (Marqeta, Lithic, Kulipa, Stripe Issuing)

requirements.quote: You run a high-velocity, disciplined delivery process. You’ve led a team that ships fast and predictably in an agile setup — sprints or kanban, versioned releases, short lead time to production — without trading away quality.

You’re agent-native. You wield agentic development — coding agents (e.g. Claude Code), MCP servers, reusable skills — as a core multiplier, with a real point of view on adopting it safely on a money product.

requirements.text: Deep in backend and distributed systems
requirements.quote: You must be deep in backend / distributed systems and genuinely literate across the rest — enough to review the work and make the architecture call in each:

Strong TypeScript / Node (or a credible senior path from Go / Kotlin / Java); you think natively in idempotency, reconciliation, retries, and consistency under partial failure, across event-driven services and Postgres.

Client-facing APIs & auth. The app-facing API as a product — versioning, idempotency keys, a clean error model — plus the auth backend behind it (OAuth2 / OIDC, session lifecycle, WebAuthn / passkeys).

Platform & reliability. Enough Kubernetes, IaC, and observability (OTel / Grafana-class) to own the deploy/rollback story and hold the reliability bar — you know the difference between a dashboard that exists and an alert that pages.
Native mobile. Enough to review a native iOS app (Swift / SwiftUI) and reason about mobile ↔ backend contracts, failure states, and on-device auth.
